title: Abigail Stops David's Revenge
overview: After Samuel dies, a rich man insults David, and David sets out to kill every male in his household until the man's wise wife, Abigail, meets him on the road and talks him out of it.

parts.label: Samuel dies (v. 1)
parts.note: Samuel, the prophet who had anointed both Saul and David, dies and the whole nation mourns him. David, now without his strongest supporter, moves deeper into the southern wilderness.

parts.label: Nabal refuses David (vv. 2-13)
parts.note: David's band had guarded Nabal's shepherds, so at sheep shearing, a time of feasting and sharing, David asked for food in return, much as desert chiefs did in much later times. Nabal, whose name means 'fool', sneers at David as a runaway servant, and David arms 400 men.

parts.label: Abigail acts (vv. 14-31)
parts.note: Warned by a servant, Abigail sends a large gift ahead, bows before David and takes the blame on herself. She urges him not to carry needless bloodshed into the kingship she expects him to receive, saying God will keep his life safe, as if tied in a bundle, but fling his enemies away like stones from a sling.

parts.label: David turns back (vv. 32-35)
parts.note: David admits he would have killed every male in Nabal's household by morning, and he thanks God and Abigail for stopping him. He accepts her gift and sends her home in peace.

parts.label: Nabal dies, David marries (vv. 36-44)
parts.note: When the sober Nabal hears how close he came to disaster, he collapses and dies about ten days later. The text says the LORD struck him, and exactly what happened to his body is unknown.

parts.label: David's wives (vv. 39-44)
parts.note: David then sends for Abigail to marry him, and we learn he has also married Ahinoam. Saul, meanwhile, has given David's first wife, his daughter Michal, to another man.

disagreement: Readers differ on whether the story mainly shows God guiding and protecting His chosen king, or also quietly exposes a darker side of David, whose 'protection' and violent oath look to some like a powerful man demanding payment.
think: What makes it possible to really hear someone who is trying to talk you out of something you feel entitled to do?
